faq.q: How long does a detail take?
faq.a: It depends on the size and condition of the car. You'll get a time window when you book.

faq.q: Do I need to be there?
faq.hint: One line: whether they need to be home, and how you get the keys (for example, keys under the mat).

faq.q: Do you need water or power from me?
faq.hint: One line: what you bring and what, if anything, you need from them.

faq.q: Can you get pet hair out?
faq.hint: One line: whether pet hair removal is included or extra, and what it costs.

faq.q: What if it rains?
faq.hint: One line: what happens to the appointment if it rains (for example, moved to the next dry day at no charge).

faq.q: How often should I get my car detailed?
faq.a: Most drivers book a full detail every few months and a quick interior clean in between. Kids, pets and long commutes mean more often.

tips: Keep a small trash bag in a door pocket and empty it every time you get gas.
Floor mats take most of the dirt. Shake them out once a week.
Park in the shade when you can: sun bakes dust and bird droppings into the paint.
Wipe spills right away; sugar and coffee stain fast in hot cars.

faq.q: Do I need to be home?
faq.hint: One line: whether they need to be home, and how you get in (a code, a key or a lockbox).

faq.q: Do you bring your own supplies?
faq.hint: One line: what you bring, and whether you'll use their products if they ask.

faq.q: What's the difference between a standard clean and a deep clean?
faq.a: A standard clean keeps a home in good shape: kitchen, bathrooms, floors and dusting. A deep clean adds the build-up spots like baseboards, inside appliances and behind furniture.

faq.q: Can I book every week or every other week?
faq.a: Yes, if you like. A recurring clean can keep the same day and time, so you don't have to rebook.

faq.q: What if I'm not happy with something?
faq.hint: One line: your redo promise, only if you offer one (for example, tell me within 24 hours and I'll come back to fix it).

faq.q: Do you clean after a move?
faq.a: Yes, move-out and move-in cleans are available. Book a few days before the keys change hands.

tips: Clean top to bottom: dust falls, so do floors last.
Let bathroom spray sit for a few minutes before you wipe; it does half the work.
A 10-minute reset every night keeps the weekend clean small.
Microfiber cloths and a squeegee beat paper towels on glass.

faq.q: How often do you mow?
faq.a: Weekly in the growing season, or every other week if your lawn grows slowly. You pick.

faq.q: Do I need to be home?
faq.a: No. We just need access to the yard: leave gates unlocked and pets inside on your day.

faq.q: What happens when it rains?
faq.a: We shift to the next dry day and let you know.

faq.q: Do you take the clippings?
faq.hint: One line: whether you bag clippings or mulch them back into the lawn.

faq.q: Do you do one-time cleanups?
faq.a: Yes. Spring and fall cleanups can be booked once, even if you don't want weekly service.

faq.q: Do you need a contract?
faq.hint: One line: how your plans work, and how a customer can stop.

tips: Mow high: cutting only the top third keeps grass thicker and greener.
Water early in the morning, deeply and less often.
Sharp blades cut clean; dull ones tear and brown the tips.
Leave the clippings when they're short: they feed the lawn.

faq.q: Will pressure washing damage my siding?
faq.a: Siding and roofs get a low-pressure soft wash; high pressure is only for concrete and other hard surfaces.

faq.q: Do I need to be home?
faq.a: No. We need an outside water spigot and clear access to the areas we're washing.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: Most driveways take an hour or two; a whole house takes longer. You'll get a time when you book.

faq.q: Is it safe for my plants and pets?
faq.hint: One line: how you protect plants and what pets should do while you work.

faq.q: How often should I wash my house?
faq.a: Once a year keeps most homes looking sharp. Shady or damp sides may need it more often.

faq.q: How do I get a price?
faq.a: Send a photo of the area and the rough size, and you'll get a price back.

tips: Clean gutters before the first big fall storm, not after.
Mildew loves the shady side of the house: check it first.
Sweep before you wash a deck; wet leaves stain.
Seal a deck a couple of days after cleaning, once it's fully dry.

faq.q: I'm a beginner. Is this for me?
faq.a: Yes. Sessions start where you are and build from there.

faq.q: Where do sessions happen?
faq.hint: One line: your studio, their home, a park or a gym, with the area.

faq.q: How often should I train?
faq.a: Two or three sessions a week is a common start. We'll set a rhythm that fits your schedule.

faq.q: What should I bring?
faq.a: Water, comfortable clothes and shoes you can move in.

faq.q: Do you help with eating habits?
faq.hint: One line: what you do and don't advise on. Leave medical advice to doctors.

faq.q: Can I try a session first?
faq.hint: One line: your intro session terms, only if you offer one.

tips: Consistency beats intensity: three steady sessions a week beat one hard one.
Sleep is training too: aim for the same bedtime most nights.
Warm up for five minutes before lifting; your joints will thank you.
Write down every workout: progress you can see keeps you going.
